$comment: The Tuxedo Touch wire contract, as observed on real hardware, expressed as data.
This file is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for tests/test_wire_contract.py, which runs the
shipped decoder against every case below. So it cannot drift from the
implementation: change one without the other and the suite fails.
It exists to be consumed by anything that must speak this protocol, including a
replacement panel server. The contract is the VENDOR's behaviour, including the
parts that are wrong - see `quirks`. A reimplementation that tidies them breaks
every client on stock firmware, which is most of them.
Verified against firmware TUXW_V5.3.21.0_VA on 2026-09-05/06.

push_stream.note: The slash before 'G.' is required; without it the server answers 404.
push_stream.encoding_note: Load-bearing. The raw 0xFE/0xFF state byte is what locates the display field; utf-8 turns it into U+FFFD and the field cannot be found at all.
push_stream.cadence_note: Measured over a 666 s hold plus two concurrent 179 s holds: 26 intervals, all between 32.68 and 33.31. The tick is GLOBAL to the panel, not per connection, so a reconnect joins a cycle already running and the FIRST gap is short and effectively random (19.30, 11.99, 14.62 observed). Never calibrate a liveness check on that first gap.
push_stream.closed_by_panel_note: Three connections across two runs ran 666 s, 179 s and 179 s and were all still open when the client gave up. No FIN, no timeout, no reset.
push_stream.concurrent_clients: at least 3; a new client does not displace an existing one, and the cadence is unbroken

rest_api.tls_note: Over port 80 every /system_http_api/ request answers 302 to https://<host>:443/tuxedoapi.html. Login still succeeds over HTTP, so a client can authenticate, issue a command, receive a plausible response, and the panel never receives it. Any reimplementation must keep this a hard failure rather than a silent no-op.

$comment: field 0  constant 0
field 1  command id
field 2  panel status code; -1 when the Tuxedo has lost its ECP link to the VISTA
field 3  state flag as hex text - PRESENT ON COMMAND 21 ONLY
field 4  raw 0xFE/0xFF byte, then colour digit, then display text
field 5  colour
The literal ':fe:'/':ff:' TEXT field appears on command 21 only (6 of 49 frames in
one capture). The RAW 0xFE/0xFF byte appears on 21 AND -1. Decode from the raw
byte: it is the more available discriminator, and it is what makes both shapes of
the -1 record work. Do not key on field position or field count - the -1 record
arrives as an 8-field partition record AND a 3-field status record.

command_ids.-1: unsolicited update; repeats whichever payload type last changed

cases.label: command 21, carries BOTH the ':fe:' text field and the raw 0xFE
command 21 arming, raw 0xFF, exit-delay countdown in the display text
command -1 status shape: RAW BYTE ONLY, no ':fe:' text field, no status code
ECP LINK DOWN: field 2 is -1 and the frame is STILL SENT, carrying the last text the Tuxedo drew
cases.note: The producer sets this field to -1 when PanelIsTalking() returns 0 and sends the frame anyway. A client that reads field 2 as a partition number discards these and reports a stale state for ever.

cases.label: command -1 partition shape: 8 fields, NO flag byte - carries no status
command 18 home partition: no flag byte, carries no status
command 504 registration data on connect: no flag byte, carries no status

rest_responses.$comment: Vendor spelling and shape preserved deliberately. 'Sucess' is misspelled in the firmware; arm returns Result.Response while disarm returns Result.Result. A reimplementation that corrects either breaks clients.

arm.means: command DISPATCHED, not code accepted. A wrong user code is presumed to dispatch identically.

status.body: empty body accepted; 'operation=get' also accepted but not required
status.quirk: Answers the literal string 'Not available' when its ECP-fed cache is empty, with no on-demand refresh. That is the defect the push stream exists to route around.

command_confirmation.$comment: The REST response confirms dispatch only. What the panel DID appears on the push stream as a change of state flag. These are the measured latencies from request to the first frame carrying the new flag.
unverified: night mode has not been observed
a declined user code has deliberately never been provoked: the panel's failed-attempt count survives a firmware reflash and three failures disable every web account
command_confirmation.no_accept_frame: sltSendUserCodeAcceptedMsg exists in the binary but a full arm/disarm cycle driven through the REST endpoints emits NO accept frame, replicated on two modes. Do not wait for one.

quirks_to_preserve: 'Sucess' is misspelled in every Status field and must stay misspelled.
Arm returns Result.Response; disarm returns Result.Result. The keys genuinely differ.
The exit-delay text has a DOUBLE space: '59  Secs Remaining'.
GetSecurityStatus capitalises its colour ('Green'); the stream sends a digit.
The push path needs the trailing slash before 'G.' or it 404s.
The stream is scoped to the panel's CURRENT partition by the producer, and carries no partition field. A multi-partition deployment must consult GetCurrentPartition rather than assume.

$comment: NOT PRESENT ON ANY FIRMWARE YET. Agreed shape, recorded here so the
integration and a replacement server are held to one document.
Stock responses below were MEASURED on TUXW_V5.3.21.0_VA, 2026-09-06.
capability_detection.session_rationale: Keeps detection structurally outside the auth path, so it can never touch the one-login budget on any firmware. Stock cannot 401 here (measured, with and without a session), and a session-required variant would 401 on custom, which this client treats as an expired session and answers with a re-login.

stock_behaviour.without_session: identical - 404 for unknown, 405 for known. Never 401, never 302.
stock_behaviour.note: 404 is the absence case. It is machine-parseable, and 405 distinguishes 'exists but wrong method' for free. The documentation-form response is specific to ARGUMENT-TAKING endpoints and does not occur for a no-argument unknown path. Unknown TOP-LEVEL paths 302 to a trailing-slash variant, which is why detection lives inside API_REV01 rather than outside it.

client_rules: contract is an integer that increments ONLY if this document's shape changes incompatibly, never for feature changes.
Branch on capabilities, never on firmware or contract.
capabilities is unordered; ignore unknown strings.
firmware and panel_model are diagnostics and device-registry material only.
Call once at setup, cache for the life of the entry, never in the poll loop.
404 means stock. It is the normal case and must be silent: no warning, no repair issue, no user-visible trace.
